question: What replaces the deterministic neural-network Gaussian-process covariance when network depth and width grow together and activation functions are shaped to avoid deep-limit degeneration?

key_findings.claim: Layerwise finite-width fluctuations remain macroscopic when depth scales with width.
key_findings.evidence: For unshaped ReLU-like networks, squared activation norms form a multiplicative Markov chain whose depth-rescaled limit is geometric Brownian motion. Pairwise correlations require a noisy discrete recursion; dropping its order-1/sqrt(width) terms, as fixed-depth infinite-width analysis does, mispredicts finite networks when depth/width is non-negligible.

anchors.section: Section 2.3, covariance and correlation Markov chains

key_findings.claim: A width-dependent activation shaping at the square-root scale produces a nontrivial stochastic covariance limit.
key_findings.evidence: For ReLU-like slopes 1+c+/sqrt(n) and 1+c-/sqrt(n), with depth d/n approaching T, the joint Gram/covariance process converges to the Neural Covariance SDE. The final network output is Gaussian conditional on this random terminal covariance, so its unconditional multi-input law is generally non-Gaussian and cannot be described by one deterministic kernel.

key_findings.claim: The square-root shaping rate is critical rather than one arbitrary convenient parameterization.
key_findings.evidence: For ReLU-like activations, slower convergence toward identity yields correlation collapse, the 1/sqrt(n) rate yields the nonlinear SDE, and faster convergence yields the linear-network SDE. A parallel trichotomy is proved for smooth activations shaped as s phi(x/s).

key_findings.claim: Smooth shaped activations admit an exact initialization norm-stability criterion under the stated joint limit.
key_findings.evidence: The diagonal covariance marginal has a finite-time explosion with nonzero probability iff three-fourths times the squared second derivative plus the third derivative at the shaping center is positive. This predicts stable centered sigmoid/tanh and a softplus threshold x0 at least log(5/4), consistent with finite n=d=100 simulations.

key_findings.claim: The theory is an initialization model, not yet a theory of learned representations, training or generalization.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion proposes posterior inference, architectural extensions and training/generalization as future work. Empirical validation compares random finite fully connected networks with the SDE rather than testing predictive gains after optimization on real tasks.

method.core_idea: Retain the layerwise stochastic fluctuations discarded by fixed-depth infinite-width limits and show that, after critical activation shaping, their cumulative joint depth-width limit is an SDE for the random Gram matrix.
method.mechanism: Express norms, covariances and correlations as Markov chains over layers; expand conditional increments through order 1/n and 1/sqrt(n); invoke functional convergence to diffusions with depth time l/n; derive drift and diffusion for ReLU-like and smooth activations; and compare simulated SDE distributions with initialized finite networks.
assumptions: Hidden-layer weights are independent Gaussian matrices and widths are equal or scale compatibly.
Depth and width jointly diverge with finite ratio d/n.
Activation functions are ReLU-like with prescribed slope scaling or C4 smooth with controlled fourth derivative.
Only a fixed finite collection of inputs is tracked.
The network is fully connected and evaluated at random initialization.
For explosive smooth cases, convergence is local/stopped rather than global.

techniques.role: Preserves the random per-layer covariance increments that accumulate over depth.
Converts layer dynamics into continuous depth/width time.
Balances nonlinearity against deep correlation degeneration.
Models the full random multi-input initialization covariance rather than a deterministic kernel.
Derives an if-and-only-if norm-stability condition for smooth shaping.

evaluations.setting: Unshaped ReLU fully connected networks with width and depth 150.
evaluations.metric: Median and final distribution of pairwise correlation.
evaluations.result: The noisy Markov recursion matches finite networks more closely than the deterministic infinite-width update.

evaluations.setting: Critically shaped ReLU-like networks with n=d=150 and 8,192 samples.
evaluations.result: The Neural Covariance SDE captures finite-network skew and spread that the sequential-limit ODE misses.

evaluations.metric: Kernel-density estimates and Kolmogorov-Smirnov convergence; occurrence of norm blow-up.
evaluations.result: SDE samples closely track finite random networks, with appendix evidence of roughly n^-1/2 convergence in a studied setting; the softplus centering criterion separates stable and unstable simulations.
evaluations.baseline: Deterministic infinite-width predictions and alternative shaping centers.

limitations: All main guarantees concern initialization; the covariance process after gradient-based training is not characterized.
The analysis is for Gaussian fully connected weights and fixed finite input sets, with only prospective extensions to ResNets/CNNs and no recurrent-network Markov reduction.
Critical shaping makes activations approach identity as width grows, so the nonlinear regime is intentionally narrow.
Smooth-activation convergence may only hold up to stopping/explosion times, and an exploded output distribution is undefined.
Simulation agreement at widths around 100-150 does not establish downstream optimization or generalization gains.
The covariance SDE posterior is not yet straightforward to compute or sample conditionally.
Depth/width joint scaling may not approximate modern heterogeneous architectures with normalization, residual paths and varying widths.
The cached source notes a repaired proof gap in an auxiliary correlation proposition, underscoring the technical sensitivity of the expansions.
failure_modes: Using a deterministic NNGP kernel when depth is comparable to width erases accumulated covariance randomness.
Choosing a shaping exponent below one-half collapses correlations or norms; choosing it above one-half removes nonlinear drift.
A smooth activation center satisfies a conventional edge-of-chaos heuristic but violates the joint-limit explosion criterion.
An SDE calibrated at initialization is misused to predict feature learning after substantial parameter updates.
Local stopped convergence is reported as an unconditional global distribution.
Finite-network architecture breaks conditional Gaussian/Markov structure through shared weights or normalization.
reusable_insights: Depth-to-width ratio should be treated as a first-class asymptotic parameter, not silently set to zero.
Track both deterministic drift and stochastic layer fluctuations when their count scales with inverse variance.
Validate initialization theories against full distributions, not just expected kernels or median correlations.
Derive activation-shaping stability analytically before numerical search.
State sequential and joint limits separately because they can yield qualitatively different covariance laws.
A random covariance mixture may be a better prior family than a deterministic Gaussian process for deep finite-width networks.
open_questions: Can the covariance SDE be extended through nontrivial training and feature learning?
How can posterior inference be performed efficiently for the random-covariance prior?
Which residual, convolutional, normalization and attention architectures retain a tractable joint limit?
Does SDE-aware activation tuning improve real training speed or generalization over deep kernel shaping?
What happens when the number of tracked inputs grows with width?
Can analogous stochastic limits predict gradients, NTKs and optimizer noise jointly?

competitive_landscape.title: Finite Depth and Width Corrections to the Neural Tangent Kernel
competitive_landscape.difference: Hanin and Nica derive finite depth/width NTK mean and variance scaling and a nontrivial first training update; the reviewed paper instead derives a full initialization covariance diffusion under activation shaping.

competitive_landscape.title: Rapid training of deep neural networks without skip connections or normalization layers using Deep Kernel Shaping
competitive_landscape.difference: Martens et al. design and empirically validate deep kernel shaping through deterministic infinite-width maps; the Neural Covariance SDE corrects that approximation when depth grows with width but does not reproduce the large-scale training study.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Learning without Shortcuts: Shaping the Kernel with Tailored Rectifiers
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. tailor leaky rectifiers and show ImageNet/CIFAR training competitive with ResNets; the reviewed paper supplies joint-limit stochastic theory and a stability criterion rather than a task-trained architecture.

competitive_landscape.title: On the infinite-depth limit of finite-width neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Hayou fixes finite width while taking residual-network depth to infinity and obtains activation-dependent diffusions, then studies the sequential width limit; this paper takes depth and width jointly to infinity in shaped feed-forward networks.

novelty_assessment: The Neural Covariance SDE is a substantive bridge between deterministic NNGP analysis and finite deep networks: it identifies the critical shaping scale, retains a full random covariance law and yields an exact smooth-activation stability condition. Its practical importance remains provisional because training, posterior inference and modern architectures are left open.
